title: Make the color space and tone mapping of bitmaps explicit
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Canvas output bitmaps, `ImageBitmap` objects, and the output bitmap of `ImageBitmapRenderingContext` have a color space, and with #11734 a tone mapping. The spec only carries both of these implicitly. `createImageBitmap()`, `transferToImageBitmap()`, and `transferFromImageBitmap()` say "a copy of" or "the same underlying bitmap data", and a note on `transferFromImageBitmap()` says that the color space and tone mapping are included in that bitmap data. No normative text gives a bitmap either property, or says what reads it.

We should make these explicit. As @ccameron-chromium described in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11734#issuecomment-6778052739, each bitmap has:

- a color space, which maps pixel values to the profile connection space (XYZ D50). In general this is an arbitrary ICC profile, which can include a 3D LUT.
- a tone mapping, which transforms those values for a target HDR headroom. In general this can be driven by a gain map image or SMPTE ST 2094-50 metadata.

So `PredefinedColorSpace` and `CanvasToneMapping` can't serve as the types. Those are only the subset a canvas context can be configured with.

This touches:

- every image source (`img`, `video`, `ImageBitmap`, `ImageData`, canvases).
- `createImageBitmap()` with `colorSpaceConversion: "none"`, which should strip both the color space and the tone mapping, but keep YUV to RGB conversion (#10578).
- `drawImage()`, which will apply the source's tone mapping once the context gets a target HDR headroom.
- serialization (#13230).
- the placeholder `canvas` element and `ImageBitmapRenderingContext` rendering paths.

This is also the internal-state part of the canvas cleanup tracked in #11163.

cc @weinig @whatwg/canvas
